title: FAR Module 3 · TBS 4

fields.label: 4. Ending Lease Liability After Year 1 Payment

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Lease Measurement

Determine the initial lease liability, right-of-use asset, interest expense, and ending lease liability.

Scenario

Orion Corp. enters into a lease on January 1.

The present value of the required lease payments at commencement is $180,000.

Orion also:

  • Makes a lease prepayment of $8,000.
  • Receives a lease incentive of $3,000.
  • Incurs qualifying initial direct costs of $5,000.

Assume the lease is classified as a finance lease.

The annual discount rate is 6%.

At the end of Year 1, Orion makes a required lease payment of $45,000.

Required

1. Initial Lease Liability
2. Initial Right-of-Use Asset
3. Year 1 Interest Expense
4. Ending Lease Liability After Year 1 Payment
explanation:
Step 1 — Initial Lease Liability

The present value of required lease payments is given as $180,000.

Initial Lease Liability = $180,000

Step 2 — Initial ROU Asset

Lease Liability $180,000 + Prepayment $8,000 + Initial Direct Costs $5,000 − Lease Incentive $3,000 = $190,000

Step 3 — Year 1 Interest

$180,000 × 6% = $10,800

Interest Expense: $10,800

Step 4 — Ending Lease Liability

Interest increases the lease liability, while the lease payment reduces it.

Beginning Liability $180,000 + Interest $10,800 − Payment $45,000 = $145,800

Ending Lease Liability: $145,800

CPA Takeaway

  • Initial lease liability is based on present value of lease payments.
  • ROU asset begins with the lease liability and is adjusted for prepayments, incentives, and qualifying initial direct costs.
  • Finance lease interest is calculated using the effective interest method.
  • Lease payments reduce the liability after accounting for interest.
